item.title: [Feature] BanyanDB: local-scan performance follow-up for tag aggregation (optional)
item.author: hanahmily
item.body:
Part 5 of 5 of the [tag aggregation and time bucketing design](https://github.com/apache/skywalking-banyandb/blob/main/docs/design/0.12.0/tag-aggregation/README.md), shipped in apache/skywalking-banyandb#1360.

**Design references:** [§7.7 The local scan: entity and indexed tags never touch the data file](https://github.com/apache/skywalking-banyandb/blob/main/docs/design/0.12.0/tag-aggregation/README.md#77-the-local-scan-entity-and-indexed-tags-never-touch-the-data-file) · [§12 Delivery order](https://github.com/apache/skywalking-banyandb/blob/main/docs/design/0.12.0/tag-aggregation/README.md#12-delivery-order) (stages 8a–9, both marked *optional* in the design)

**Depends on:** #14089 (time-bucket grouping) and #14090 (COUNT_DISTINCT) — this optimizes both. Not required for either to ship; the design explicitly defers this and asks that the payoff be measured before it's built.

## Scope

**Phase A — run-folding** (design's "intermediate step," no new execution path)
- Fold each maximal `(series, bucket)` span once instead of per row, using a plan-time flag marking which key columns are index-resolved — derived from `searchSeriesList`'s existing three-way projection split, never inferred at runtime by sampling column values.
- Applies whenever an index-resolved tag is a group key: `COUNT_DISTINCT` collapses `n − 1` redundant set inserts per span into one; `COUNT` becomes `count += spanLength`.

**Phase B — metadata-only scan** (after Phase A lands)
- Bypass block decode entirely when *every* tag the query touches (group keys, aggregation target, any tag a residual predicate touches) resolves from the series index — gated by the range-containment guard (a block whose `[min,max]` isn't fully inside the query range must still read `timestamps.bin`) and the no-residual-predicate guard.
- `index_mode` measures are the structural first case: they hold no part-resident tags at all, so an index-mode aggregation is index-only by construction.

## Out of scope
- Anything that changes correctness or the query surface — this issue is pure performance, gated by differential tests against the existing (already-correct) path.

## Test / Definition of done
- Phase A: differential test against the unoptimized per-row path on the same fixture (identical results, fewer group-map probes); a magnitude assertion (an 8192-row block at hour buckets collapses to ~137 spans, not 8192 key computations).
- Phase B: differential test against the decoding path across both index-mode and part-backed fixtures (identical results); the range-containment fixture — a block with rows at 09:00 and 09:59 (one hourly bucket) queried over 09:30–09:31 must yield no bucket row, while the same block fully inside the query range takes the shortcut.

output.title: perf(measure): fold tag-aggregation spans by (series, bucket) instead of per row
output.summary: The vectorized BatchAggregation.Consume operator (pkg/query/vectorized/measure/aggregation.go) recomputes the group key and re-probes the group map for every row, even when every tag-derived group-by key is index-resolved (an entity or indexed tag that searchSeriesList's three-way projection split already proves constant across one series) and the rows form a contiguous (series, bucket) span — wasting n-1 key computations, map probes, and (for COUNT_DISTINCT) redundant idempotent set inserts per span. The fix adds a plan-time index-resolved flag per group-by key, carried from the analyzer's existing entity/indexed-tag classification into the operator (never inferred at runtime by sampling column values), and changes Consume to resolve the group once per maximal (series, bucket) span — reusing the span boundaries BatchTimeBucket already detects while scanning for bucket advances — whenever every tag-derived key in that span is index-resolved: COUNT becomes count += spanLength and COUNT_DISTINCT becomes one set insert when the aggregation target is also index-resolved, while SUM/MIN/MAX/MEAN keep folding per row but skip the now-redundant key recomputation. This fix is scoped to Phase A (run-folding) only; Phase B (bypassing block decode entirely for a metadata-only scan) is the issue's own next phase, explicitly sequenced "after Phase A lands," and is deferred to a follow-up. No wire format, API, or default-behaviour change is introduced; correctness is pinned by a differential test against the existing, unoptimized per-row path on the same fixture, plus a magnitude assertion on span count.

test.name: TestBatchAggregation_RunFoldingMatchesPerRowPath
test.expectedValueSource: Two independent oracles, both outside the new code path: (1) row-for-row equality against the existing, unmodified per-row Consume path run on the identical input batch/fixture — the issue's own DoD ("differential test against the unoptimized per-row path on the same fixture, identical results"); (2) a magnitude assertion computed by arithmetic stated directly in the issue text — an 8192-row single-series batch at 1-minute cadence with hour-wide buckets must collapse to ~137 spans (8192 rows / 60 rows-per-hour ≈ 137), not 8192 key computations. Allocation-count comparison (testing.AllocsPerRun) between the folded and per-row paths on the same input serves as the "fewer group-map probes" proxy, since design doc §7.7 identifies computeKey's string(buf) escape as exactly one heap allocation per row today.

output.productionCaller: pkg/query/vectorized/measure BatchAggregation.Consume, invoked by the BuildOperators-constructed GroupByAgg operator for both standalone measure queries and the data-node map phase (AggModeMap) of distributed measure queries, whenever the query's group-by keys resolve to entity or indexed tags.

decisions.point: Whether to implement Phase A (run-folding) and Phase B (metadata-only scan) together or scope this fix to Phase A only.
options: Implement both phases in one PR
Implement Phase A only; Phase B as a follow-up
decisions.chosen: Implement Phase A only; Phase B as a follow-up
decisions.basis: The issue itself sequences them — "Phase B — metadata-only scan (after Phase A lands)" — and the design's §12 delivery table lists stage 9 as "optional, after 8a". Each phase has its own differential-test gate and its own correctness surface (Phase B bypasses block decode entirely, a new execution strategy per §7.7: "a separate execution strategy, not a tweak... belongs after the main design lands"). Bundling them violates the smallest-reversible-change default.

decisions.point: Precise condition under which a (series, bucket) span may be folded into one key resolution.
options: Fold whenever any index-resolved tag is a group key (the issue's loose summary phrasing)
Fold only when every tag-derived group-by key in the query is index-resolved (design §7.7's precise invariant)
decisions.chosen: Fold only when every tag-derived group-by key is index-resolved
decisions.basis: Design doc §7.7 states the span is maximal "sharing (series, bucket)" only, with no caveat for a mix of resolved/unresolved keys. If any group-by key column were part-resident (able to vary row-to-row within one series+bucket), the key would not be constant across the span, and resolving the group once would silently merge rows that belong in different groups — the exact correctness regression the issue's "Out of scope: anything that changes correctness" forbids. The design document outranks the issue's shorthand per the sources priority (linked design document over issue prose).

decisions.point: Whether collapsing COUNT to count+=spanLength and COUNT_DISTINCT to one set insert additionally requires the aggregation TARGET column (not just the group-by keys) to be index-resolved.
options: Collapse whenever the group key is index-resolved, regardless of the target column's resolution
Require the target column to also be index-resolved before collapsing the per-row aggregate application; otherwise keep the per-row aggregate loop (still reusing the once-resolved group)
decisions.chosen: Require the target to also be index-resolved
decisions.basis: Design §7.7's table is explicit: "COUNT_DISTINCT over a series-constant target → one set insert" (emphasis on series-constant target, not just key). A part-resident COUNT_DISTINCT/COUNT target can legitimately differ row-to-row within one (series,bucket) span (e.g. a non-indexed tag), so collapsing to one set-insert or spanLength in that case would under/over-count. When the target isn't index-resolved, the span-folding still saves the key/map-probe work (group resolved once) but the aggregate step itself stays a per-row loop over that one resolved group — matching the table's SUM/MIN/MAX/MEAN row ("still per row — but the key work is saved"), generalized to any non-index-resolved target.

decisions.point: Mechanism for carrying the plan-time index-resolved flag from the analyzer into the aggregation operator.
options: A bool slice/bitmask attached to the existing plan-level aggregation spec (populated once at plan-build time from searchSeriesList's existing three-way split)
A separate runtime lookup consulted at operator-construction time
decisions.chosen: bool slice on the existing plan-level spec, populated once at plan build time
decisions.basis: The issue is explicit: "a plan-time flag... derived from searchSeriesList's existing three-way projection split, never inferred at runtime by sampling column values." This matches the existing pattern already in the codebase for per-column plan-time metadata on the aggregation spec (TagFamily, HideTag per design §7.1), so it is the smallest, most consistent addition.

decisions.point: Whether Phase A needs a new feature flag / config gate.
options: Ship unconditionally, relying on the differential test for correctness confidence
Gate behind a new config flag
decisions.basis: Design §7.7 explicitly distinguishes the two phases: Phase A/run-folding "needs no new execution strategy at all, only a change inside the aggregation operator," whereas only Phase B is described as "a separate execution strategy... belongs after the main design lands, gated on a differential test." Adding a flag for Phase A would be a larger public surface than either the issue or the design calls for, and the repo's own convention (e.g. BANYAND_TRACE_NATIVE_WIRE) reserves flags for genuinely alternate execution paths, not internal per-row-vs-per-span folding inside one operator.

decisions.point: How to verify the "fewer group-map probes" requirement without adding test-only instrumentation to production structs.
options: Add a counter field/hook to BatchAggregation for tests to read
Use testing.AllocsPerRun / allocation-count comparison as a proxy, since the per-row cost is a stated heap allocation
decisions.chosen: Use an allocation-count proxy via testing.AllocsPerRun
decisions.basis: Design §7.7 names the per-row cost precisely: computeKey's string(buf) "escapes" at the function boundary, i.e. one heap allocation per row today. Comparing allocations-per-op between the folded and per-row paths on the same fixture measures exactly that waste using an idiomatic Go testing mechanism, avoiding a new test-only field on BatchAggregation.

decisions.point: Reach: which callers and lifecycle paths depend on BatchAggregation.Consume's current per-row semantics and must remain correct under span-folding.
options: Audit only the standalone part-backed query path
Audit standalone, the distributed data-node map phase, and index-mode's non-streaming aggregator, plus Close/budget-release behaviour
decisions.chosen: Audit standalone + distributed map-phase + index-mode, and Close/budget-release
decisions.basis: BatchAggregation is constructed once by BuildOperators for both standalone GroupByAgg queries and the data-node map phase (AggModeMap) of distributed queries — same operator, same Consume, so a span-folding bug corrupts both deployment shapes identically (the same silent-wrong-number risk class §7.4 calls out for COUNT_DISTINCT). Index-mode queries also build a BatchAggregation-shaped non-streaming aggregator (§7.2), but index-mode batches arrive one-row-per-index-entry (copyTo builds a single-timestamp MeasureResult per §7.7's own caveat), so a multi-row span may not occur there at all; the existing index-mode-ordering test (§11: timestamps arriving A, B, A) already exercises Consume on index-mode batches and needs no change, but the new differential test must additionally run its fixture through the index-mode path to confirm folding is inert (a no-op) there rather than assuming it. Close is unaffected: folding only changes which rows resolve to an already-created group within one Consume call; it does not change the once-per-group MemoryTracker charge/release in Close (§7.6) since folding reduces re-resolutions of the same group rather than creating new ones, and introduces no new goroutine, I/O, or cancellation-sensitive wait — the span is bounded by the existing maxBlockLength=8192 per-block cap. Risk: no existing test asserts on live group-resolution call counts (only output-row equality is tested today per §11), so the new test must add that assertion itself rather than relying on coverage that doesn't yet exist.

followUps: Phase B: metadata-only scan — bypass block decode entirely when every tag the query touches (group keys, aggregation target, any tag a residual predicate touches) resolves from the series index, gated by the range-containment guard and the no-residual-predicate guard, with index_mode measures as the structural first case (design §7.7, issue's own 'Phase B').

Confirm whether index-mode's PullBatch batch shape ever presents multi-row single-series spans that Phase A's run-folding could actually help, per design §7.7's caveat ('the batch-oriented PullBatch path for index mode should be checked before assuming it benefits') — i.e. verify Phase A is inert rather than a missed opportunity on that path.

Benchmark/confirm the SUM/MIN/MAX/MEAN key-folding side-benefit (group resolved once per span even though the aggregate itself still loops per row) that falls out of the same mechanism for free, per design §7.7's table.

output.summary: The plan correctly captures Phase A (run-folding) of apache/skywalking#14092. It is grounded in design §7.7 and §12 (delivery stage 8a), takes the conservative correctness path (fold only when ALL key columns are index-resolved, and require the target to be index-resolved before collapsing COUNT/COUNT_DISTINCT — matching the design's table at §7.7), stays inside one operator with no new execution path, and defers Phase B (metadata-only scan) as a follow-up. Decisions are well-tiered (all implementation) and basis-ed (design doc + repository pattern). Reach is mostly self-contained: Consume's per-row work is the only changed behavior, no new groups, no change to budget/reservation/Close, AggModeReduce uses combinePartial (unaffected), BatchTimeBucket continues to flush per bucket in streaming mode. The differential test design (row-equality + testing.AllocsPerRun proxy + the design-stated 137-span arithmetic) is the right shape for the issue's DoD.

findings.detail: pkg/query/vectorized/measure/reduce.go:148 — NewBatchAggregation(refSchema, keyIndices, specs, AggModeReduce, ...) is the reduce-phase caller. Its AggModeReduce path uses combinePartial (not fold), so run-folding has no effect on it; but the plan's reach audit does not explicitly enumerate this caller. The reach decision (point 7) covers "standalone + distributed map-phase + index-mode" but skips the liaison reduce. Either list it explicitly with "uses combinePartial, no fold, no effect" or note that the new constructor parameter can default to "all false" so the call site does not change.

pkg/query/vectorized/measure/aggregation.go:234 (NewBatchAggregation) is called from BuildOperators (plan.go:155), BuildTimeBucketOperator (timebucket.go:163, 372) and ReducePartialBatches (reduce.go:148), plus ~25 test sites (aggregation_test.go). Adding a non-optional parameter would force changes at every test site. The plan's decision 4 mentions "a bool slice on the existing plan-level spec" but doesn't say whether the NewBatchAggregation signature changes (and how tests are kept green). The least-disruptive shape is to store the flag as a BatchAggregation field set via a setter or as an extra (zero-default) parameter, so legacy callers default to "no folding" and existing tests remain untouched.

The plan describes the magnitude assertion as "stated directly in the issue text." The 137-spans arithmetic is actually in design §7.7 (line 1166 of docs/design/0.12.0/tag-aggregation/README.md), not the issue body. This is acceptable — the design document outranks the issue and the arithmetic is testable from it — but the source attribution is slightly off. Also, an 8192-row single-series batch is bench-shaped, not unit-shaped; the existing tests in this package use 3–9 row fixtures. Consider framing it as a benchmark (b.Run with row count) rather than a hard assertion in a Test function, or scale down while preserving the proportionality.

The plan's "maximal (series, bucket) span" framing implies scanning for sub-Consume boundaries. In practice, BatchTimeBucket already splits per bucket via flushCurrentBucket (timebucket.go:316–325, design §7.2 + §7.7), so within any single BatchAggregation.Consume call in streaming mode the bucket is already constant; the entire active[] is one span. Non-bucketed Consume sees one series per batch by construction (BuildMeasureBatchFromResult). So the fold reduces to "if all keys index-resolved → resolve the group once for the entire active[]". This is correct, just slightly over-described; the actual implementation is simpler than the plan's wording suggests.

The plan refers to "the existing, unmodified per-row Consume path" as the differential-test oracle. The row-based engine was actually removed (#1326; design §8 confirms "no row-path analyzer left"). What remains as a row-equivalent is rowSerialize in diff_test.go:100 (a faithful re-implementation of the row-path serializer in test code), which TestDiff_* already uses. The plan should acknowledge that the differential oracle is this test-side re-implementation, not a live row-path code path — this matters for honesty about where the cross-check comes from.

The plan's index-resolved flag must be derived at plan-build time from the measure schema's entity tag names and indexed-field locations. Today pkg/query/vectorized/measure/plan/analyzer.go does not consult schema.GetEntity().GetTagNames() or any fieldIndexLocation (grep finds no hits); that plumbing is part of plan scope. Not a blocker — the analyzer has the measureSchema pointer (analyzer.go:269 — measureSchema.GetIndexMode()) and the entity info is on the same struct — but the analyzer-side work is implicit in the plan and should be called out so the implementer doesn't treat "derive from searchSeriesList's three-way split" as if searchSeriesList runs in the vec path (it runs in banyand/measure/query.go, before vec dispatch).

output.summary: The plan correctly scopes Phase A only (run-folding), follows design §7.7's invariants, and uses idiomatic mechanisms. However, two correctness-critical details in Consume's span detection are not specified: (1) how the implementation detects (series, bucket) boundaries inside Consume when the input is multi-series (the index-mode map-mode path feeds all rows in one Consume call, with rows potentially from different series), and (2) how AggModeReduce's per-row markDedupSeen interacts with span-level folding. The follow-ups acknowledge both but defer verification rather than nail them down before the test. The plan must specify the boundary-detection algorithm (and test the part-resident-key / multi-series non-foldable case) before approval.

findings.detail: pkg/query/vectorized/measure/timebucket.go:334 (map-mode feedRun) and pkg/query/vectorized/measure/aggregation.go:362 (Consume loop). In the index-mode map-mode path, BatchTimeBucket.consumeBatch feeds ALL active rows as a single Consume call (no bucket-boundary chunking, unlike streaming). For an index-mode batch built by indexSortResult.mergeSegResultsBatch (banyand/measure/query_batch.go:261-291) where rows from different series are placed in the same MeasureBatch, one Consume call can include rows from multiple series — and those rows have DIFFERENT group keys (entity tags differ per series). A naive implementation that treats the whole Consume call as one foldable span will collapse rows that must stay in different groups, exactly the silent-wrong-number correctness regression the issue forbids. The plan's follow-up #2 acknowledges this ('Confirm whether index-mode's PullBatch batch shape ever presents multi-row single-series spans that Phase A's run-folding could actually help') but defers verification rather than resolving it. The plan must specify the (series, bucket) boundary-detection algorithm used inside Consume — either by walking the timestamp and series columns for boundaries (mirroring BatchTimeBucket.consumeBatch's streaming loop), or by explicitly disabling folding when the input batch contains more than one series / more than one bucket. The plan must also state the test for this non-foldable case. Without it, a future implementation can regress correctness silently.
findings.finding: Consume must detect (series, bucket) boundaries; the plan does not specify how

findings.detail: pkg/query/vectorized/measure/aggregation.go:388 (markDedupSeen call in Consume). AggModeReduce currently calls markDedupSeen per row to drop rows that share (shard_id, group_key). If span-folding is applied to the reduce path too — which the plan does not explicitly exclude — then markDedupSeen must be hoisted to span granularity. The plan's reach audit lists AggModeReduce as in scope of the audit ('the resulting direction has the same silent-wrong-number risk class §7.4 calls out for COUNT_DISTINCT') but does not state whether span-folding actually engages for AggModeReduce or stays limited to AggModeAll/AggModeMap. The plan must clarify. (The test name TestBatchAggregation_RunFoldingMatchesPerRowPath and the description do not mention AggModeReduce, suggesting the implementation is restricted to AggModeAll/AggModeMap — but the reach section explicitly includes Reduce in the audit. This contradiction must be resolved.)
findings.finding: AggModeReduce + markDedupSeen + span-folding interaction is unspecified

findings.detail: pkg/query/vectorized/measure/aggregation.go (Consume path). The plan's regression coverage (TestBatchAggregation_RunFoldingMatchesPerRowPath, differential test on the same fixture, plus a magnitude assertion for an 8192-row block at hour buckets) only exercises the foldable case where every tag-derived key is index-resolved. It does not specify a regression test for the NON-foldable case — a (series, bucket) span where a tag-derived group-by key is part-resident and therefore varies row-to-row within the span. Without this negative test, a future implementation that mistakenly folds even part-resident-key rows would pass the foldable differential test and silently merge rows that belong in different groups. The plan must include this negative-case test. (Same fixture works: a part-resident tag key creates two distinct groups within the span; folded output must NOT collapse them.)
findings.finding: No regression test for the non-foldable case (part-resident key varies within span)

findings.detail: pkg/query/vectorized/chunked_consume.go (ConsumeChunked). ConsumeChunked chunks a batch at the batchSize boundary, which can split a single (series, bucket) span across two Consume calls. If run-folding detects spans inside Consume and computes the key per-span, the fold can no longer span across ConsumeChunked chunks. For the part-file path with batchSize=4096 and a block of 8192 rows with one bucket, the first Consume call sees rows 0-4095 (folded), the second sees 4096-8191 (folded) — the fold still works, just per-chunk. For the index-mode path with multi-series/multi-bucket input, ConsumeChunked's chunking is independent of (series, bucket) and could split a series-per-row span across calls. The plan should clarify how folding handles ConsumeChunked chunks. (Likely: the fold can simply restart per chunk, which is a worst-case no-op for the optimization but still correct.) This is minor because correctness is preserved; only the optimization's payoff is reduced.
findings.finding: ConsumeChunked's chunk boundary may split a (series, bucket) span

output.summary: The plan implements Phase A (run-folding) only — the issue's optional first stage — deferring Phase B (metadata-only scan) per the design's explicit "after Phase A lands" sequencing. It correctly identifies the root cause: per-row `computeKey` produces a heap-allocating string per row, plus N-1 redundant map probes (and N-1 redundant hash probes for COUNT_DISTINCT), all of which the design §7.7 "intermediate step" says can be folded when the group key is constant across a (series, bucket) span. The plan's decisions are appropriately conservative: it requires every tag-derived group-by key AND the aggregation target to be index-resolved before collapsing the per-row aggregate application, which matches the design §7.7 table; it ships unconditionally with no new flag (correct since Phase A is "no new execution strategy at all"); it uses testing.AllocsPerRun as the "fewer group-map probes" proxy per design §7.7's identification of computeKey's string(buf) as exactly one heap allocation per row; it correctly identifies all call sites (standalone, distributed map-phase, index-mode map, Close) and pins down what evidence the new test must produce (the index-mode-ordering test only exercises Consume on index-mode batches today; the new test must additionally verify folding is inert on that path, not assume it). The test name fits the `TestBatchAggregation_*` pattern and the magnitude assertion (8192 rows / 60 rows-per-hour ≈ 137 spans) is taken directly from the issue text.

findings.detail: Plan-time derivation of the index-resolved flag is described as drawn from "searchSeriesList's existing three-way split," but pkg/query/vectorized/measure/plan/analyzer.go's Analyze(req, measureSchema, mode) signature does not currently receive index rules — only AnalyzeDistributed does. The same Entity/Indexed-vs-part-resident classification is derivable from measureSchema.GetEntity() plus the indexRules slice, but the plan does not spell out where the resolution happens (most likely a new optional indexRules argument on Analyze, or resolving it in dispatch.go before Build). This is an implementation gap the implementer must close, but it does not change correctness or visible behaviour.

The plan's phrasing "COUNT_DISTINCT collapses n − 1 redundant set inserts per span into one" is slightly imprecise: foldDistinct already gates on Contains(encoded), so the n-1 redundant calls are hash+probe operations returning true, not redundant *inserts* (which would allocate). The design doc §7.7 explicitly calls them "idempotent no-ops that still pay a hash and a probe each," so the underlying intent (N redundant hash probes collapse to one) is correct; the plan's wording conflates insert with probe. Magnitude is unchanged.

item.detail: The test fixture's exact numeric expectation is "~137 spans" but 8192/60 = 136.53, so the actual span count depends on the starting minute within the bucket (could be 136, 137, or a partial-leading edge). The plan should assert a tolerance (e.g. spans >= 136 && spans <= 137) rather than equality to avoid flakiness on edge alignments. This is a one-line test polish, not a design concern.

output.summary: Plan correctly scopes Phase A only (per issue's sequencing), applies the right-most-conservative rule for COUNT/COUNT_DISTINCT collapse (target must be index-resolved), and matches design §7.7's invariant that every tag-derived group-by key must be index-resolved. Mechanism (plan-time bool slice on the existing spec) fits the existing pattern. Test name and package fit the convention. Two blocking issues remain: (1) the plan's text says BatchTimeBucket "already detects" the boundaries that Consume reuses, but BatchTimeBucket only does this in streaming mode — in map mode the persistent aggregator can see multi-bucket batches in one Consume call, so Consume itself must do bucket-advance scanning for the bucketed-map path to fold safely; (2) the plan claims "fewer group-map probes" as a test assertion but the chosen mechanism is `testing.AllocsPerRun` as a proxy — the plan needs to state this proxy explicitly in the test description, since the design §7.7's exact text is "fewer key computations, allocations and map probes" (not directly count-spans). A minor issue: the productionCaller doesn't explicitly note AggModeReduce is inert (no multi-row spans to fold there), which is fine but should be acknowledged.

findings.detail: In pkg/query/vectorized/measure/aggregation.go BatchAggregation.Consume (and the related BatchTimeBucket.feedRun in pkg/query/vectorized/measure/timebucket.go), the plan says it reuses span boundaries BatchTimeBucket already detects. This is only true in streaming mode (consumeBatch's bucket-advance loop at timebucket.go:341-358 splits into same-bucket runs before feedRun). In map mode (streaming=false, set by resolveTimeBucket for index-mode measures), consumeBatch calls feedRun once with the entire active[] (timebucket.go:333-334), so a Consume call may receive a multi-bucket batch even though all rows are from one series. Without bucket-advance scanning inside Consume for that path, the plan would either (a) silently merge rows from different buckets into one group when keys are index-resolved (a correctness regression the issue explicitly forbids), or (b) miss the fold opportunity. The plan needs to add explicit bucket-advance scanning inside Consume for the case where bucketIdx>=0 and streaming-mode split is not upstream.

The plan's test.description says "fewer group-map probes" and "an 8192-row block at hour buckets collapses to ~137 spans, not 8192 key computations" but the chosen mechanism is `testing.AllocsPerRun` as a proxy (per the plan's own decision #6) because design §7.7 names the per-row cost as exactly one heap allocation from `string(buf)` escape. Direct span-counting would require test-only instrumentation, which the plan rejects. The test description should explicitly state it uses AllocsPerRun as the proxy for both "fewer group-map probes" and the 137-spans claim (8192 rows × ~1 alloc/row ≈ 8192 allocs in the unoptimized path; ~137 in the optimized path — a 60× signal well above noise). Without that clarification, an implementer might add a test-only counter to BatchAggregation to make the magnitude assertion literal, undoing decision #6.

The plan's chosen mechanism (decision #4) says "bool slice on the existing plan-level aggregation spec". The implementation needs (a) per-key bools (one per entry in keyIndices, parallel to it), and (b) a target-index-resolved bool (parallel to AggSpec). The decision's wording suggests a single bool slice; in practice that means two parallel slices or a struct with both fields. Decision #4 should clarify whether the per-key flag and the per-target flag are one combined spec field or two — for consistency with the existing HideTag per-AggSpec pattern, two (one per AggSpec for target, one per keyIndices for keys) is the cleaner fit. Not blocking: any consistent choice works.

The plan's productionCaller says BatchAggregation.Consume is hit for standalone + distributed map phase (AggModeMap). AggModeReduce is also constructed by ReducePartialBatches in pkg/query/vectorized/measure/reduce.go:148, and uses the same Consume. Reduce batches contain one row per (shard, group) — there are no multi-row same-key spans, so folding is naturally inert there (the index-resolved flag is never set for the key columns of a reduce batch in the way that produces a multi-row span). The plan should note this explicitly so an implementer doesn't accidentally enable folding in AggModeReduce by checking only the flag and not the batch shape. Not blocking because the natural shape already makes it inert.

The issue says Phase A "Applies whenever an index-resolved tag is a group key: COUNT_DISTINCT collapses n−1 redundant set inserts per span into one; COUNT becomes count += spanLength." The plan's decision #3 narrows this to "require the target column to also be index-resolved" — more conservative than the issue's literal text but consistent with design §7.7 and necessary for correctness (a part-resident COUNT target can be null on some rows in a span; `count += spanLength` would then over-count). This is a correct narrowing; it should be recorded as a planned divergence from the issue's shorthand rather than presented as a direct reading of the issue. Not blocking.

prior.finding: In pkg/query/vectorized/measure/aggregation.go BatchAggregation.Consume, the plan's claim that it reuses span boundaries BatchTimeBucket already detects is only true in streaming mode — in map mode Consume can see multi-bucket batches and must scan for bucket advances itself.
prior.reason: The plan needs to add explicit bucket-advance scanning inside Consume for the case where streaming-mode split is not upstream. The issue's correctness constraint and the design's table make this load-bearing.

prior.finding: The test description should state it uses testing.AllocsPerRun as the proxy for both 'fewer group-map probes' and the 137-spans magnitude claim, since direct span-counting would require test-only instrumentation the plan rejects.
prior.reason: The test must work via the chosen mechanism (decision #6), not via the text's literal phrasing. The plan's wording is inconsistent.

output.summary: Plan implements the right Phase A scope with conservative aggregation rules, but two issues block approval: (a) the plan-time flag plumbing for indexed tags is not named — the standalone Analyze signature has no access to index rules, only to entity tag names on the proto; (b) the "count += spanLength" rule for COUNT skips the per-row null check, which is a correctness regression for COUNT over nullable int64/float64 fields and any COUNT over an index-resolved string/bytes tag (a "✅ new" cell in design §6 that explicitly excludes nulls in existing tests).

findings.detail: pkg/query/vectorized/measure/plan/analyzer.go Analyze signature is (req, *databasev1.Measure, mode); the proto Measure carries EntityTagNames directly but NOT index rules. Indexed-tag classification in the runtime path (banyand/measure/query.go:searchSeriesList) needs (entity, families, *indexRules, indexMode) via partition.ParseIndexRuleLocators — the standalone analyzer never sees indexRules today. The plan claims "a bool slice on the existing plan-level spec, populated once at plan build time" but does not specify the channel: BuildContext carries no index rules, GroupByAgg holds no derived set, and Analyze's signature would need to change OR BuildContext would need to carry a derived per-key flag set. Either choice is a non-trivial API change that the plan must name.

pkg/query/vectorized/measure/aggregation.go:fold() does `if col.IsNull(rowIdx) { return nil }` before incrementing for COUNT, and the same check happens implicitly via appendKeyComponent for COUNT_DISTINCT. The plan's rule "COUNT becomes count += spanLength" does not account for per-row nulls: index-resolved targets can be null (query.go:489 maps out-of-range entity offsets to pbv1.NullTagValue; mustDecodeTagValue maps nil to NullTagValue). For COUNT over an int64/float64 nullable field or any COUNT over an index-resolved string/bytes tag (design §6 "✅ new" cells, with TestBatchAggregation_CountDistinct_ExcludesNulls pinning null-exclusion behavior), "count += spanLength" silently over-counts. The plan must either (a) walk the span's null bitmap to count non-nulls before incrementing, or (b) restrict it to column kinds for which null is precluded (and document the restriction).

BatchAggregation has four entry points that need the new index-resolved flag: NewBatchAggregation itself, the schema-only probe in GroupByAgg.Schema (groupby_agg.go), openBucket in BatchTimeBucket (timebucket.go:372), and ReducePartialBatches (reduce.go:148). The plan's decision paragraph names only the design pattern (TagFamily/HideTag on the aggregation spec); it should also name that BatchTimeBucket.openBucket and reduce.go's ReducePartialBatches inherit the flag from the surrounding plan/scratch batch, since both call NewBatchAggregation independently and a per-key column-aware derivation needs to flow through them.

testing.AllocsPerRun measures heap allocations only — design §7.7's named per-row waste is "string(buf)" escaping to heap (1 alloc/row), which AllocsPerRun captures. But the issue's "fewer group-map probes" claim is about pure-CPU work that AllocsPerRun does NOT capture; a deterministic per-batch counter (counting computeKey calls, group-map probes, distinct inserts) would directly assert the magnitude claim rather than inferring it from allocation counts. The plan should either add a counter as a test-only field or accept AllocsPerRun as a proxy and document why the proxy is sufficient.

Design §7.7 explicitly cautions that index-mode "the multi-row single-series batch that run-folding collapses may not arise on that path" and "the batch-oriented PullBatch path for index mode should be checked before assuming it benefits." The plan correctly defers Phase B (metadata-only scan) but does not name an index-mode inertness assertion in the Phase A test. The plan's followUps list mentions verifying it is inert on the batch path — should make this a test gate, not just a follow-up, since run-folding changes Consume unconditionally and a no-op on index-mode batches needs to be confirmed, not assumed.

prior.reason: Confirmed: Analyze(req, *databasev1.Measure, mode) does not receive indexRules; only AnalyzeDistributed does. The plan's claim that the flag is "derived from searchSeriesList's existing three-way projection split" is partially true for entity tags (proto-accessible) but not for indexed tags (requires ParseIndexRuleLocators(entity, families, indexRules, indexMode) which is not currently called in the standalone analyzer).

prior.finding: count += spanLength skips per-row null check, which the existing fold path performs via col.IsNull(rowIdx) for COUNT and via appendKeyComponent returning dst unchanged for nulls in COUNT_DISTINCT
prior.reason: Confirmed: banyand/measure/query.go maps out-of-range entity offsets and nil field values to pbv1.NullTagValue, so an index-resolved target CAN be null. The plan's "count += spanLength" rule applies regardless of nullability.
